metaDescription: CPT 99491 explained: CCM time personally performed by a physician or qualified practitioner. Time threshold, rules, pairing with 99437 and 2026 rate.
summary: CCM reported when the physician or other qualified practitioner personally spends at least 30 minutes in the month on care management, instead of clinical staff time.
time: 30 minutes personally performed by the practitioner per month
performer: The physician or other qualified practitioner personally
frequency: Once per patient per calendar month
requirements: Two or more chronic conditions expected to last at least 12 months or until death, with significant risk of decline
Practitioner time only; clinical staff minutes do not count toward this code
Documented consent and a comprehensive care plan
A time log attributing the 30 minutes to the practitioner
pitfalls: Counting staff time toward the practitioner's 30 minutes
Billing 99491 and 99490 for the same patient in the same month
conflicts: Not reported in the same month as 99490 or 99487 by the same practitioner.

faqs.question: Why do most practices bill 99490 rather than 99491?
faqs.answer: 99490 uses clinical staff time, which scales without taking practitioner hours. 99491 requires the practitioner's own time, so it suits low-volume cases.

faqs.question: Can staff minutes count toward 99491?
faqs.answer: No. Only the physician's or qualified practitioner's own time counts for this code.
